A jetting nozzle directs pressurized water into a line to break up and flush material such as grease or sludge. It may clean more of the pipe interior when repeated clogs come from wall buildup. Roots can grow through an open joint, and a cable or jet may clear the immediate blockage without closing that opening. If backups recur or several fixtures are affected, a camera inspection can help locate the cause and show whether repair is the better next step.

In older parts of Lawrence, a line may be clay or cast iron with joints that have shifted over time. That can favor an inspection first, so the cleaning method fits the weakest part of the pipe rather than the newest.
